findings.title: isAccessTokenId() matcher has wrong substring offset and inverted comparison logic
findings.body:
In `isAccessTokenId(String expectedGrantShortcut)`, the matcher does:
```
if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
```
Two separate bugs here:
1. The grant-type shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the 6-character context prefix (positions `[4,6)`), not `[3,5)`. For a token id like `onrtac:...`, `substring(3,5)` yields `"ta"`, not the grant shortcut `"ac"`.
2. Even ignoring the offset bug, the condition is inverted: the method should return `false` (fail the match) when the shortcut does NOT equal the expected value, but it currently returns `false` only when it DOES equal it.

As a result, this matcher almost never fails regardless of which grant type is actually encoded in the token id (since `substring(3,5)` virtually never matches `expectedGrantShortcut`, the `if` never triggers and the method falls through to `isUUID()` on the raw id, effectively ignoring the grant-type check entirely). All tests using `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectAuthReqIdToToken`, etc. that rely on this matcher do not actually verify the new token-id encoding feature, defeating the purpose of the added assertions and potentially masking real encoding bugs.

findings.title: Duplicate null-check validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId
Javadoc for getShortcut() contradicts the fixed 2-character format enforced by the encoder
findings.body: The javadoc states: "@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants ... Shortcut should be unique across grants." However, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider`/`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` hard-code a fixed 2-character length for the grant-type segment (e.g. `encodedContext.substring(4, 6)` and the overall length check `encodedContext.length() != 6`). All built-in grant factories indeed return exactly 2 characters, which contradicts the "3-letters" documentation. If a developer follows the javadoc and implements a 3-character shortcut for a custom grant type, the fixed-length assumptions in the encoder will break (the encoder will produce malformed ids, and decoding of its own just-generated token ids will throw IllegalArgumentException due to the length-6 check).

findings.title: No validation that OAuth2GrantTypeFactory shortcuts are exactly 2 characters, risking self-generated tokens becoming undecodable
findings.body: `postInit()` collects grant-type shortcuts from all `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations without verifying their length. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` simply concatenates the session/token/grant shortcuts assuming each is exactly 2 characters, and `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` enforces a strict 6-character total length for decoding. If any (built-in or third-party) `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` implementation returns a shortcut that isn't exactly 2 characters (which the javadoc actually suggests is acceptable, e.g. 3 characters), tokens generated with that grant type will fail decoding later (e.g. in introspection or revocation code paths that call `getTokenContextFromTokenId`), throwing `IllegalArgumentException("Incorrect token id ... Expected length of 6")` for tokens the server itself just issued.

findings.title: New abstract method added to existing provider factory interface without a default implementation
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added as a new abstract method on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, which extends `ProviderFactory`. Any existing custom/third-party implementation of this SPI (e.g. a custom grant type extension) will now fail to compile/deploy until it implements this new method, since no default implementation is provided. Given this is meant to be an extensible SPI (the PR description explicitly states "provider adds ability for someone to introduce his own provider"), this is a breaking change for existing extensions without a deprecation/default-method migration path.

findings.title: Access token jti format change is an unannounced/unflagged contract change with no opt-out
findings.body: `initToken()` now always runs the generated token id through `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()`, changing the shape of the `jti` claim for every access token from a plain UUID to a prefixed value like `onrtac:<uuid>`. Any external tooling, logging/correlation systems, or internal code (admin REST API, introspection consumers, custom SPI implementations) that assumes the access token id is a canonical UUID (e.g. checks length 36, applies UUID regex, or compares it against other UUID-shaped identifiers) will now break. There is no configuration flag/toggle shown to disable this new encoding for backward-compatibility, and no migration note is provided for deployments relying on the previous token id format.
